description: Review EDIS Digital Immune System (DIS) and determine what to build FIRST for our WordPress site going live on nginx. We built: Go ring buffer (internal/dis/ring.go), fingerprint engine (header-order hash + session HMAC + threat scoring), HTTP middleware harvester, 4-state posture engine (healthy/elevated/attack/degraded with 30s rolling windows), ad mode selector (svg/text/pow_captcha/none), collector daemon (cmd/dis) tailing nginx access logs + exposing :9099/dis/health. WordPress plugin edis-dis: reads collector health via WP transients (10s TTL, fail-open to svg), [edis_dis_ad] shortcode, admin posture panel. Full spec: EDIS/docs/digital-immune-system.md. Site not live yet — S23-01 (deploy WordPress) is next. Think hard: minimum DIS stack to ship NOW for real protection? What can wait? Hidden failure modes? First 24h watch list? One design mistake to fix before deploying?
acceptance_criteria: Ranked list: DIS component to ship first, second, third for WordPress+nginx
Assessment: collector-daemon log-tailing approach right for WordPress+nginx, or better first path
Top 3 hidden failure modes in current DIS design
First 24h monitoring checklist once EDIS goes live
One thing we got wrong that should be fixed before deploying
context: EDIS is WordPress+nginx+PHP-FPM+MySQL. DIS tails nginx logs -> health state -> WordPress plugin adjusts ads. Pre-launch. Strategy: SHANKPIT(S19)->AskEmily(S20-21)->DataLicensing(S22)->EmilyBrain(S22+). EDIS must go live for data licensing to have a public face. DIS is protective but cannot delay launch. Key axiom: fail open always. We just built the full DIS stack (ring buffer, fingerprint, posture engine, collector daemon, WordPress plugin). What is the tightest viable first deploy?
